scenario_user_message: Should I build a portfolio project first, or grind interview questions first?

finalMessages.content: Should I build a portfolio project first, or grind interview questions first?

content.text:
That's partly a portfolio-strategy question, so let me stay in my lane and answer the sequencing part, then point you to the right node.

Here's the honest framing: for AIPM interviews specifically, the two aren't really substitutes. A portfolio project isn't just a resume line — it's the raw material you'll draw on in the interview itself. AIPM interviews lean heavily on "tell me about a time you shipped/scoped/evaluated something." If you grind questions with no real project behind you, your answers stay generic and interviewers notice fast.

So the sequencing I'd push: get at least one substantive project in motion *before* you go deep on interview drills, because the project gives you the stories and the technical fluency the drills test. You don't need it fully polished — you need enough lived experience to speak concretely.

But the actual "how to build the project" — what to build, how to make it prove AIPM ability — that belongs to your **Portfolio** sibling node. Go there for the project design.

What I can help with here: what the interviews actually test, so you know what the project needs to arm you for. Do you know the rough shape of an AIPM loop yet — the round types you're likely to face?
